etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English generosite, from Latin generōsitās.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) The trait of being willing to donate money, resources, or time.

quote.citation: 1963, Erik H. Erikson, Childhood and Society:
quote.text: We have mentioned generosity as an outstanding virtue required in Sioux life.

quote.citation: 2013 June 14, Jonathan Freedland, “Obama's once hip brand is now tainted”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 1, page 18:
quote.text: Now we are liberal with our innermost secrets, spraying them into the public ether with a generosity our forebears could not have imagined. Where we once sent love letters in a sealed envelope, or stuck photographs of our children in a family album, now such private material is despatched to servers and clouds operated by people we don't know and will never meet.

quote.citation: 1873, Reverend M. C. Tyler, Proceedings at the Laying of the Corner Stone of the Sage College of the Cornell University:
quote.text: May the generosities of the founders of these halls, be rewarded by the fair and holy characters which shall be here formed […] .

definitions.definition: (uncountable) The trait of being abundant, more than adequate.
(archaic, uncountable) Good breeding; nobility of stock.
